- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 10-day high), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.  
- Model consistently overestimates in early forecast horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply 1–2% downward bias for first 7 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast > 70% of recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days; if below, increase by 1–2%.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply downward bias.
